items.title: Tamil Nadu library scam: DVAC arrests proprietor of Akal Vizhakku Publishers R Mohan
items.summary: The Directorate of Vigilance and Anti-Corruption (DVAC) has arrested R Mohan, proprietor of Akal Vizhakku Publishers and Phoenix Publications on Monday, November 16, over irregularities in procuring books for public libraries, including the Periyar Arivulagam Library in Coimbatore. In the First Information Report (FIR), registered on November 15, the agency said that books were created under fictitious author names, contained misleading information and were procured through collusion between the publisher and government officials. Besides Mohan, the FIR also names unidentified officials from the Directorate of Public Libraries, Anna Centenary Library in Chennai and Periyar Arivulagam Library in Coimbatore. The irregularities resulted in payments totalling more than Rs 1.74 crore to two publishing firms, the agency said. The irregularities came to light after writer Perumal Murugan flagged inaccuracies and fabricated historical and literary references in books stocked at the newly inaugurated Periyar Arivulagam Library in Coimbatore. Perumal Murugan identified nearly 1,800 allegedly dubious books bearing the imprint of Agal Vilakku Pathippagam and more than 100 books published by Phoenix in 2023 at the library. He raised concerns about fictitious authors, questionable historical claims, factual inaccuracies and the possibility that some content was generated by AI. According to the FIR, the irregularities came to light during a detailed inquiry initiated after a request from the School Education Department Secretary on November 6. The Madurai Bench of the Madras High Court had also directed the DVAC to register an FIR in the matter on November 10. The inquiry covered the procurement of books and e-books for six libraries: Periyar Arivulagam in Coimbatore, Kamarajar Arivulagam in Tiruchy, Bharathidasan Arivulagam in Salem, Anjalai Ammal Arivulagam in Cuddalore, Quaid-E-Millath Arivulagam in Tirunelveli, and libraries in six newly formed districts. The FIR alleged that the government had sanctioned Rs 50 crore for procuring books and e-books for the Periyar Arivulagam Library through a Government Order dated September 3, 2024. Administrative approval for the amount was granted on February 27, 2026, and an advance of Rs 30 crore was released from the Consolidated Fund. items.title: TVS family dispute: What the law says about a daughter’s inheritance rights
items.summary: The dispute within the TVS family over the distribution of its assets among the next generation took a legal turn on Monday, with Dr Lakshmi Venu sending a notice to her father and TVS Holdings Chairman Venu Srinivasan. Through the legal notice, Lakshmi has called for a “fair and lawful partition” of the assets of the Venu Srinivasan branch of the Chennai-based TVS family, and contends that “the concentration of beneficial interest in favour of her (younger) brother,” Sudarshan Venu, was to the exclusion of her own lawful rights. Lakshmi is the MD of auto parts maker Sundaram-Clayton, with a market cap of over Rs 2,000 crore, while Sudarshan is the chairman and MD of two-wheeler maker TVS Motors, which has a market cap of over Rs 2 lakh crore. Sudarshan is also MD of TVS Holdings, the holding company, which is headed by their father, Venu. Venu’s wife, Mallika Srinivasan, is the chairperson and MD of tractor manufacturer TAFE, where Lakshmi is vice-chair. In April last year, Venu named his son and current CMD of TVS Motor, Sudarshan, as the Significant Beneficial Owner. This would mean that he would inherit the larger portion of the businesses and assets of TVS Holdings. Lakshmi contends that no settlement of the assets within her immediate family was ever initiated, and says that she is being wrongfully denied her rightful share of the joint family property. Citing the Hindu Succession Act 1956, which now recognises daughters as equal inheritors of property in an undivided Hindu family, Lakshmi has asked her father to “discharge his fiduciary duties” and effect a fair and lawful partition.
